arxiv-2006-10002.title: Lattices over Bass rings and graph agglomerations
arxiv-2006-10002.creator: Nicholas R. Baeth, Daniel Smertnig
arxiv-2006-10002.description: Abstract . We study direct-sum decompositions of torsion-free, finitely generated modules over a (commutative) Bass ring R R through the factorization theory of the corresponding monoid T ⁡ ( R ) T(R) . Results of Levy–Wiegand and Levy–Odenthal together with a study of the local case yield an explicit description of T ⁡ ( R ) T(R) .

arxiv-2103-15593.title: Multi-source Transfer Learning with Ensemble for Financial Time Series Forecasting
arxiv-2103-15593.creator: 1 st Qi-Qiao He, 2 nd Patrick Cheong-Iao Pang, 3 rd Yain-Whar Si
arxiv-2103-15593.description: Abstract Although transfer learning is proven to be effective in computer vision and natural language processing applications, it is rarely investigated in forecasting financial time series. Majority of existing works on transfer learning are based on single-source transfer learning due to the availability of open-access large-scale datasets.

arxiv-2108-09371.title: Investigation of the Relation between Space-Weather Parameters and Forbush Decreases Automatically Selected from Moscow and Apatity Cosmic Ray Stations during Solar Cycle 23.
arxiv-2108-09371.creator: J. A. Alhassan, O. Okike, A. E. Chukwude
arxiv-2108-09371.description: Abstract We present the results of an investigation of the relation between space-weather parameters and cosmic ray (CR) intensity modulation using algorithm-selected Forbush decreases (FDs) from Moscow (MOSC) and Apatity (APTY) neutron monitor (NM) stations during solar cycle 23. Our FD location program detected 408 and 383 FDs from MOSC and APTY NM stations respectively.

arxiv-2108-13538.title: Stability of Self-similar Solutions to Geometric Flows
arxiv-2108-13538.creator: Hengrong Du, Nung Kwan Yip
arxiv-2108-13538.description: Abstract We show that self-similar solutions for the mean curvature flow, surface diffusion and Willmore flow of entire graphs are stable upon perturbations of initial data with small Lipschitz norm. Roughly speaking, the perturbed solutions are asymptotically self-similar as time tends to infinity.

arxiv-2207-11529.title: Low-complexity CNNs for Acoustic scene classification
arxiv-2207-11529.description: Abstract This paper presents a low-complexity framework for acoustic scene classification (ASC). Most of the frameworks designed for ASC use convolutional neural networks (CNNs) due to their learning ability and improved performance compared to hand-engineered features. However, CNNs are resource hungry due to their large size and high computational complexity. Therefore, CNNs are difficult to deploy on resource constrained devices.

arxiv-2212-12157.title: Contact Angle Hysteresis on Rough Surfaces Part I: Mechanical Energy Balance Framework
arxiv-2212-12157.creator: Dalton J.E. Harvie 1
arxiv-2212-12157.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Dalton J.E. Harvie 1. Using as a starting point conservation of momentum, a multiphase mechanical energy balance equation is derived that accounts for multiple material phases and interfaces present within a moving control volume. This balance is applied to a control volume that is anchored to a three phase contact line as it advances over the surface of a rough and chemically homogeneous solid.

arxiv-2308-04028.title: Top K Relevant Passage Retrieval for Biomedical Question Answering
arxiv-2308-04028.creator: Shashank Gupta
arxiv-2308-04028.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shashank Gupta. I
Abstract

Question answering (QA) is a task that answers factoid (what, when, where, etc.) questions using a large collection of documents. It aims to provide precise answers in response to the user’s questions in natural language. Question answering relies on efficient passage retrieval to select candidate contexts, where traditional sparse vector space models, such as TF-IDF or BM25, are the de facto method.

arxiv-2411-05031.title: On-Device Emoji Classifier Trained with GPT-based Data Augmentation for a Mobile Keyboard
arxiv-2411-05031.creator: Hossam Amer, Joe Osborne, Michael Zaki, Mohamed Afify
arxiv-2411-05031.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hossam Amer, Joe Osborne, Michael Zaki, Mohamed Afify. Emojis improve communication quality among smart-phone users that use mobile keyboards to exchange text. To predict emojis for users based on input text, we should consider the on-device low memory and time constraints, ensure that the on-device emoji classifier covers a wide range of emoji classes even though the emoji dataset is typically imbalanced, and adapt the emoji classifier output to user favorites.

arxiv-2504-12681.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) trained on extensive datasets often learn sensitive information, which raises significant social and legal concerns under principles such as the “Right to be forgotten.” Retraining entire models from scratch to remove undesired information is both costly and impractical.

arxiv-2505-01064.title: Efficient Vocabulary-Free Fine-Grained Visual Recognition in the Age of Multimodal LLMs
arxiv-2505-01064.creator: Hari Chandana Kuchibhotla, Sai Srinivas Kancheti, Abbavaram Gowtham Reddy, Vineeth N Balasubramanian
arxiv-2505-01064.description: Abstract Fine-grained Visual Recognition (FGVR) involves distinguishing between visually similar categories, which is inherently challenging due to subtle inter-class differences and the need for large, expert-annotated datasets. In domains like medical imaging, such curated datasets are unavailable due to issues like privacy concerns and high annotation costs.

britannica-1911-fender.title: Fender (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-fender.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-fender.description: Article 'Fender' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 10), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. When the open hearth with its logs burning upon dogs or andirons was replaced by the closed grate, the fender was devised as a finish to the smaller fire-places, and as a safeguard against the dropping of cinders upon the wooden floor, which was now much nearer to the fire. Fenders are usually of steel, brass or iron, solid or pierced.

pmc-10671007.title: Suitability of the Attitudes to Aging Questionnaire Short Form for Use among Adults in Their 50s: A Cross-Sectional e-Survey Study
pmc-10671007.creator: Gail Low, Alex Bacadini França, Donna M. Wilson, Gloria Gutman, Sofia von Humboldt
pmc-10671007.description: This cross-sectional e-survey study examines the suitability (reliability and validity) of the 12-item Attitudes to Aging Questionnaire Short Form (AAQ-SF) for use among adults in their 50s. The AAQ-SF instrument was originally designed to capture subjective perceptions of physical change, psychosocial loss, and psychological growth by asking people aged 60 and beyond how they feel about growing older.

pmc-10704754.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing in cancer research: discovering novel biomarkers and therapeutic targets for immune checkpoint blockade
pmc-10704754.creator: Boyu Sun, Ziyu Xun, Nan Zhang, Kai Liu, Xiangqi Chen, Haitao Zhao
pmc-10704754.description: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has become a promising strategy in treating advanced cancers, providing significant survival benefits for patients with various cancer types. However, among the vast population of cancer patients, only a small fraction are able to respond to and derive benefits from ICB therapy.

pmc-11464756.title: Lake water storage changes and their cause analysis in Mongolia
pmc-11464756.creator: Huihui Zhao, Baojin Qiao, Haiyan Liu, Xiaohui Chen, Yi Xiao, Guofeng Wang
pmc-11464756.description: Lake is an important water resources in Mongolia, which has undergone a large variation in past decades. However, it is still challenging to monitor long-term changes in lake water storage (LWS) due to the lack of lake level monitoring and long-term satellite altimetry data for Mongolian lakes.

pmc-11678540.title: Helicobacter pylori Inhibition, Gastritis Attenuation, and Gut Microbiota Protection in C57BL/6 Mice by Ligilactobacillus salivarius NCUH062003
pmc-11678540.creator: Junyi Li, Xiaoyan Xu, Shiyu Yang, Kui Liu, Min Wu, Mingyong Xie, Tao Xiong, Jun-Hyung Cho
pmc-11678540.description: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori), one of the most prevalent pathogenic bacteria worldwide, is the leading cause of gastritis, gastric intestinal metaplasia, and gastric cancer. Antibiotics, the conventional treatment for eliminating H. pylori, often lead to severe bacterial resistance, gut dysbiosis, and hepatic insufficiency and fail to address the inflammatory response or gastric mucosal damage caused by H. pylori infection.

pmc-12447899.title: Indoor airborne carcinogen synergy in children: systematic interdisciplinary approach to PM2.5-nicotine driven lung tumorigenesis and targeted intervention
pmc-12447899.creator: Boyu Pan, Xiwen Feng, Fujian Jiang, Rui Li, Han Zhu, Kunpeng Wang
pmc-12447899.description: Graphical abstractThis study integrates environmental engineering and bioinformatics to explore nicotine and PM2.5-induced lung cancer risks in children. Introduction Indoor air pollution emerges as an urgent and significant challenge to global health, contributing to the deaths of 3.2 million individuals in 2020 alone, including over 237,000 children under the age of five (World Health Organization, 2021).

pmc-12645723.title: The effect of the COVID-19 pandemic on racial disparities in suicide and homicide by firearm rates in Missouri
pmc-12645723.creator: Samuel Kim, Rithvik Talluri, Audrey Yu, Megan Evans, Apurva Bhatt
pmc-12645723.description: Missouri homicide rates rose during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020–2023), spiking in 2022. Data obtained from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention database showed from 2018 to 2023, Black/African American American youth experienced the most firearm-related homicides before and during the pandemic. This study also found demographic differences between youth firearm suicide and homicide rates in Missouri.

pmc-13425955.title: Succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency: exploring the relationship between ALDH5A1 variants and molecular effect on SSADH
pmc-13425955.creator: Dandan Yan, Xiangyu Liu, Chunyu Gu, Yingzi Cai, Wenxuan Fan, Chunhua Zhang, Dong Li, Jianbo Shu, Hanjie Wang, Chunquan Cai
pmc-13425955.description: BackgroundSuccinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD), caused by variants in ALDH5A1, is a rare inherited neurometabolic disorder with phenotypic heterogeneity. To clarify the pathogenicity of ALDH5A1 variants, we systematically investigated their effects on succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH) structure and function.MethodsWe obtained the clinical and molecular characteristics of 12 probands.
